findings.description: The implement gate now selects 'authoritative' mode solely from `.loa.config.yaml` (`implement_gate.mode`). In that mode the gate trusts `tool_input.active_skill`, which the header comment itself acknowledges is model-authored (the PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill field). `.loa.config.yaml` sits at the project root and is not an App-Zone path, so a Write/Edit to it passes this very hook unconditionally (non-App-Zone writes always allowed). Chain: the agent writes `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` into `.loa.config.yaml`, then emits `active_skill: implement` in subsequent Write/Edit tool_input to bypass the fail-ask fence on App-Zone writes outside /implement or /bug.
findings.failure_mode: C-PROC-001 fence (fail-ask on ungated App-Zone writes) is bypassable by the governed agent once the operator-only opt-in flag is set by a path the gate does not fence; the 'authoritative' label overstates the trust that a model-authored field deserves.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove authoritative mode until the harness exposes a non-model-authored skill indicator, or treat `.loa.config.yaml` (and `implement_gate.*` specifically) as a fenced path in this hook and the System-Zone hook; at minimum, in authoritative mode still require corroboration from the heuristic .run/ RUNNING state before allowing, and log an audit event when active_skill is honoured.

findings.description: hook-guard.sh fails OPEN (exit 0, tool allowed) when the wrapped safety hook fails `bash -n`. The diff widens its documented scope to SessionStart hooks and keeps the fail-open posture for PreToolUse fences. Hook files live under `.claude/hooks/` and the constraints text in this same diff concedes that Bash-path writes to protected zones are an accepted fence gap, so a Bash-path edit that introduces a syntax error into implement-gate.sh (or any wrapped fence) silently disables that fence for the rest of the session.
findings.failure_mode: A single corrupted or truncated hook file converts every wrapped PreToolUse safety hook into a no-op with only a stderr warning, which the model may not surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail CLOSED (or fail-ask) for PreToolUse fences while keeping fail-open for SessionStart; alternatively, emit a structured permissionDecision 'ask' with the parse error so the human sees the degraded state rather than a silent allow.

findings.description: The new `anthropic:claude-headless` registry row statically declares `file_write: false`, `command_execution: false`, `network_access: false` and `execution_mode: remote_model`, but its own note admits the adapter runs a local `claude -p` process whose tool surface is widened by `extra.allowed_tools` in model-config.yaml. The permissions registry and the catalog are not cross-checked, so an operator (or a later catalog edit) can grant the headless hop Write/Bash tools while the trust registry still asserts a side-effect-free oracle. The new parity test only checks that a row exists and mirrors 4.7 scopes; it does not verify the catalog's `extra.allowed_tools` is empty.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream consumers of model-permissions.yaml (trust scopes, red-team/flatline routing) make decisions on a capability posture that can diverge from the actual process capability of the headless hop.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an assertion (e.g. in test_trust_scopes.py or the catalog floor tests) that `providers.anthropic.models.claude-headless.extra.allowed_tools` is empty or absent whenever the registry row claims `command_execution: false`/`file_write: false`, or derive the row's capabilities from the catalog at load time.

findings.description: The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. In the requirement loop, `rule_key "$perm"` is called as a bare statement; `rule_key` returns 1 for any rule that is not of the form `Bash(...)`. If `all_required` ever contains a non-Bash requirement (e.g. a Read/Edit rule), the whole preflight aborts mid-loop instead of reporting that rule, so the remaining required permissions are never checked. The previous `base_pattern_of` helper never returned non-zero, so this is a new failure path introduced by the grammar refactor. Also, for an exact (non-wildcard) requirement the derived base becomes `*=<cmd>`, which can never match an allow or deny key.
findings.failure_mode: A preflight that is supposed to surface missing or denied Bash permissions exits abnormally; depending on the caller, this is either a hard stop or a silently skipped check, and exact-form requirements are never covered by a wildcard allow.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the call: `rule_key "$perm" || { missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; }` and compute the base only when the key starts with `*` (wildcard requirement), or normalise the requirement list to wildcards at definition time.

findings.description: The evidence recorder runs before the file_path check, i.e. on every Write/Edit invocation, and on first sight of a model-authored `tool_input.active_skill` it rewrites `.run/platform-features.json`, merging in `active_skill_available: false`. That unconditionally clobbers whatever detect-platform-features.sh (changed in this PR but truncated from the review) previously recorded for that key. The write is triggered by model-controlled input, so the model can decide when the lead session's platform-features state is rewritten. Content is constrained to fixed strings and a timestamp, so there is no injection, but the recorder is a model-triggerable write into lead-only `.run/` state.
findings.failure_mode: Any other consumer of `active_skill_available` sees it flip to false after the first model-authored active_skill field, and the write occurs regardless of whether the tool call targets a fenced path.
findings.suggested_fix: Record only `active_skill_seen_at`/`active_skill_source` without touching `active_skill_available`, move the recorder after the file_path/App-Zone checks, and have detect-platform-features.sh own the `active_skill_available` key exclusively.
